newsitem.title: USA: NY police find explosives in apartment raid.
newsitem.headline: NY police find explosives in apartment raid.

text.p: Police found explosive devices in an early morning raid on a New York apartment on Thursday and arrested three "Middle Eastern" men, two of whom were shot and wounded, officials said.
The bomb squad search of the apartment turned up what appeared to be some type of pipe bomb, police sources said, but city and federal officials declined to comment on the nature of the devices.

"We don't know exactly what this is at this point, but obviously the investigation is continuing," James Kallstrom, the head of New York's FBI office told a news conference at City Hall. "There are a lot of leads, we're not going to talk about those."

Police ordered the raid after receiving a tip at 10:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday (0245 GMT Thursday), New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said. He said police entered the ramshackle apartment at 4:40 a.m. EDT Thursday (0840 GMT) and found three men sleeping inside and the devices.

"The individuals involved are Middle Eastern but we don't have definite confirmation of their nations of origin yet," the mayor told reporters at the site of the discovery in the residential Park Slope neighbourhood of Brooklyn.
Giuliani later said at the City Hall news conference that the shootings occurred when one of the men in the apartment appeared to reach for an object as the raid was in progress.

"They had reason to believe that at least one or possibly both men were in the process of activating a bomb," Giuliani said. "It may turn out that they were, it may turn out that this device isn't, but in any event that's what they thought was going on."
The two wounded men were being treated at the King's County hospital but their injuries were not life-threatening, officials said.
The Mayor said police officers found an unspecified number of explosive devices, "as many as two possibly activated."

Agents from the New York bomb squad, the FBI Joint Terrorist Task Force and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms cordoned off a four-block wide area around the apartment, evacuated residents and diverted subway services.
The subway runs underneath the building where the suspected explosive devices were found. Giuliani said the devices had been safely removed and were being inspected.

"The FBI and the Joint Terrorism Task Force, which is a task force composed of state and local and federal agencies in and around the city of New York, (are) working on it. They're working together," U.S. Attorney-General Janet Reno said in Washington.
The raid created chaos for residents in the neighbourhood as police awoke them in the early hours. About 90 people were evacuated from their homes.

"I was sleeping and they were banging on the doors," said resident Evita Carabello, who lives in an apartment building near the one that was raided. "They were yelling and yelling 'you have to leave, leave the house now because there's a bomb'."
Four subway lines were diverted by the investigation, leaving hundreds of thousands of commuters seeking alternative transport.
